_doc: Headwaters source registry - Delhi episodic sources. Schema + design notes: docs/specs/headwaters.md (local). Delhi's live-feed story is unusual: its highest-cadence public source (DPCC monthly river + drain analysis) publishes as scanned PDFs on a Drupal listing, so edition detection here is what tells us a new month exists - the extraction itself is manual/OCR until that pipeline lands. MANUAL WATCH (not automatable here): the CGWB observation-well network behind public/data/delhi-cgwb-stations.json stopped reporting on 2025-09-20. Resumption would restore Delhi's only high-cadence groundwater signal, but it cannot be expressed as a registry check - the India-WRIS Ground Water Level endpoint needs a POST with mandatory query params, and while dormant it returns an empty array, so any api-date datePath would error rather than report no-change. Re-run neer-vazhvu-api/scripts/build_delhi_cgwb_stations.py --refresh to test.

sources.refreshMethod: manual (new month's river/drain/STP PDFs -> transcribe into dpcc-monthly-wq-delhi.json, then re-run scripts/build-delhi-river-quality.ts)
sources.notes: THE Delhi feed: 8 Yamuna stations + ~39 drain points + STP compliance, sampled monthly and published around the 25th. A new file link = a new month. The drain 'NO FLOW' count in each edition is the verification instrument for the drain-trapping commitment. Feb-2026 is absent from the listing - confirm whether that is a publication gap when the next editions land.

sources.license: open (per OpenCity dataset page); underlying assessment is CGWB + state GW departments
sources.refreshMethod: manual (add the new edition's Delhi district CSV URL to neer-vazhvu-api/scripts/build_delhi_gwr_blocks.py and re-run; if the edition is not mirrored, pull it from IN-GRES directly - see docs/methodology/pan-india-source-playbook.md)
sources.notes: Assessment is annual since 2021-22. IN-GRES (ingres.iith.ac.in) is the authority and is reachable outside NICNET; OpenCity mirrors most editions. The 2022-23 cycle had no mirror and was taken from IN-GRES itself (public/data/ingres/delhi-2022-2023.json). Watch for the next cycle appearing here or on the portal's year list.

sources.refreshMethod: manual (a new DJB performance/compliance audit -> update cag-djb-audit-2025.json, the dashboard hero stats and the commitments register)
sources.notes: Report No. 3 of 2025 (tabled 23 Mar 2026) is the audit-grade spine of Delhi's dashboard: NRW 51-53%, Rs 4,988 cr revenue impact, Rs 66,595 cr debt, 40% of production billed. A follow-up or compliance audit would move several headline numbers at once.

sources.refreshMethod: manual (new edition's water chapter -> refresh source-wise availability split + the 'wasted or pilfered' figure in delhi-supply-overview.json)
sources.notes: Chapter 13 carries DJB's own source-wise raw-water split (Yamuna/Ganga/Bhakra/groundwater) and the state's own '52.35% wasted or pilfered by tanker mafia' line. Published annually alongside the Delhi budget.

sources.refreshMethod: manual (new monthly bundles -> extend delhi-cetp-monthly-index.json; bulk values await the OCR batch)
sources.notes: Per-CETP inlet/outlet monitoring across 23 parameters incl. heavy metals, plus measured flow vs design capacity and the plant's OLMS status. Archive currently ends Nov 2024 - new resources here would mean the series resumed.
